definition: Third-person perspective is an outside-observer viewpoint used when people judge or react to another person’s situation rather than imagining themselves directly in it. In this research context, it contrasts with first-person perspective during moral judgment tasks.

reasons: The definition’s claim that third-person perspective is “an outside-observer viewpoint” is not explicitly supported by the packet text.

The definition’s claim that it is used “when people judge or react to another person’s situation” is not explicitly supported; the packet only states that participant perspective differs (first-person vs third-person) in moral reactions/dilemmas.

The phrase “In this research context, it contrasts with first-person perspective during moral judgment tasks” is only partially supported: the packet describes stimuli/perspective differences for first- vs third-person (and mentions moral judgments generally), but it does not clearly specify “moral judgment tasks” as a defined contrast in the sense used by the definition.

The packet only supports a research usage contrasting first-person and third-person perspective in moral judgment tasks; it does not define third-person perspective as an outside-observer viewpoint or as judging another person’s situation more generally.
The wording extends beyond the packet by presenting a broad conceptual definition rather than the narrower experimental usage described in the source.
